reasons: Clearing and writing a table is not atomic.

terms.meaning: A database built into the browser that stores data on the user's device.
A helper library that makes IndexedDB easier to use.
A list of changes made offline that waits to be sent to the cloud.
Save a record: update it if it exists, otherwise insert it.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Loads the local database library and the cloud connection.
sections.why: Needed for local storage and syncing.

sections.name: SyncQueueItem
sections.title: Sync queue entry shape
sections.what: Describes one waiting change: which table, what action, which record, the data and when it happened.
sections.why: Lets offline changes be saved and sent later.
sections.watch_out: The data field is loosely typed, so nothing checks it is correct before it is sent.

sections.name: MomentumDatabase, db
sections.title: Local database definition
sections.what: Defines the browser database and one table for each area of life, plus the sync queue, and exports one shared copy.
sections.why: Likely reason: local storage for offline use.
sections.watch_out: The name says v2 but the schema is version 1. Reason not stated. Any change to table indexes needs a new version number.

sections.name: loadStateFromDexie
sections.title: Load all local data
sections.what: Reads every table at once and returns them together, or returns nothing if reading fails.
sections.why: Likely reason: one fast read at startup.
sections.watch_out: A null result means the caller must handle the empty case, or the screens will look blank.

sections.name: saveCollectionToDexie
sections.title: Replace a table with a list
sections.what: Empties one local table and writes the new list into it.
sections.why: Likely reason: simple full save of one area.
sections.watch_out: Clearing and writing are two steps, so an interruption between them can leave the table empty.

sections.name: queueOfflineMutation
sections.title: Queue a change for later
sections.what: Adds a record to the sync queue with the current time so it can be sent when online.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps offline edits safe.
sections.watch_out: A failure here is only logged, so the change can be lost without the user knowing.

sections.name: processSyncQueue
sections.title: Send queued changes to the cloud
sections.what: When online and signed in, sends each queued insert, update or delete to the cloud, and removes it from the queue after success.
sections.why: Likely reason: pushes offline work up when the connection returns.
sections.watch_out: Items that keep failing stay in the queue and retry every time, with no limit.

summary: Manages the app's local database in the browser so data is kept offline, and queues changes to send to the cloud later.
purpose: Lets the app work without a connection and keeps a list of changes waiting to be synced.
why: Likely reason: the browser database lets the app load instantly and survive offline use.
how: 1) Defines the local database and one table per area of life, plus a sync queue table. 2) Loads all tables into one object at startup. 3) Replaces a table's contents when saving. 4) Adds changes to the queue when offline. 5) Sends queued changes to the cloud when online and signed in.
inputs: Saved data from the app stores, changes to queue, and the signed-in user id.
outputs: Loaded app data, saved local tables, and changes pushed to the cloud.
risks: Clearing and rewriting a table is not one step, so an interruption can leave it empty. Errors are logged but not shown. Failed queue items retry with no limit.
debug: Open the browser developer tools and look at the IndexedDB storage named MomentumOS. Check the console for lines that start with Failed or Error syncing. If data vanishes after a save, look at the clear and write step.
